summary.headline: Bajaj Finance Q1 FY27: ROE 20.4% and ROA 4.7%, profit up 28%, record INR37,000 crore AUM addition; management holds FY27 guidance for one more quarter.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as an excellent quarter across volume momentum, new customer additions (5 million) and profitability, with profit growth of 28% and ROE above 20%. Loan loss to average AUF improved to 1.54% from 1.87% a year ago, but included a INR296 crore management and macro overlay; excluding it, the figure would be 1.31%. Opex to NTI rose to 33.4%, attributed to gold loan and MFI branch expansion and the new labour code. Management declined to revise FY27 guidance, saying it would revisit after Q2, and said the company is prioritising balance-sheet resilience.

financial_highlights.change: vs 1.87% in same period last year

financial_highlights.change: marginally higher YoY; new labour code 10 bps (INR60 crore)
added 1,650 (811 excluding gold loan and MFI)
ROE up from prior; opex to NTI from 21%; AUM up 24%, disbursements up 33%

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM grew 112% and is about 4% of AUM; branches are at 1,700 with 110 added per month, targeting 2,700-2,800 (possibly 3,000) by year-end and FY27 AUM of INR29,000-31,000 crore. Digital platform contributes about 25% of gold loan business.

segments.name: Rural and urban consumer finance
segments.commentary: Grew 49% and 38% respectively; about half of the ~40% average growth is SKU price increases, about 20% organic. Management flagged further SKU price increases from OEMs. Smartphone ticket size up 32-33% YoY.

segments.name: MSME / business loans
segments.commentary: MSME grew 2% as risk-driven pruning since July 2025 continues; management expects return to growth by about Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Bajaj Housing Finance (BHFL)
segments.commentary: Record quarterly AUM addition, disbursements up 33%, AUM up 24%, PAT and PBT up 23%, ROE 12.5%, GNPA 0.29% and NNPA 0.12%; intense competition causing attrition pressure.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv Securities (BFSL)
segments.commentary: Strong AUM growth with profit growth softer at 22%; management says the business is maturing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 22-24% unchanged; management says Q1 is better than March guidance but wants one more quarter before revising.
Opex to NTI expected to improve 25-40 bps for FY27 despite Q1 at 33.4%.
Margin moderation of 10-15 bps expected at this juncture for FY27 (Sandeep Jain's guidance reiterated by Rajeev Jain).
Credit cost: management optimistic on FY27 outlook; guidance revision deferred to Q2.
Cost of funds expected to stay range-bound with slight upward bias, given West Asia crisis and monsoon risks; incremental cost up an estimated 30-60 bps in fixed income markets.

BHFL dilution to 75% from 86.7% (company holds 21% stake in BHFL) is the first capital protocol; no capital raise planned for now. Dividend payout expected to lift Q2 ROE. Management term decision by Dec 2027-Jan 2028.
capex_capacity: Gold loan network: 1,700 branches today (only 80 integrated legacy); 110 branches added per month; peak capacity about INR37,000-38,000 crore at 2,800 branches (about INR14 crore per branch at maturity).
Non-gold-loan and MFI branch network flat or declining over last 7-8 quarters; plan to open about 160 branches in FY27 and 170-250 annually, with 4-5% distribution expansion.
AI unit expanding from 230 to 400 people; 300 added to digital platform unit; digital platform to deliver INR50,000 crore business this year and management targets INR100,000 crore next year.

Custom AI model to go live in Q2 for B2B (0.5 million customers); B2C version by October-November; new consumer AI platform by May-June 2027; two new lines of business planned for January-February 2027.
Balance sheet expected at INR630,000-650,000 crore by year-end.
demand_pricing: Competition across all lines for 3-4 years from PSU banks, private banks and NBFCs; management says it is nothing new.
Gold loan competition rising, but management cites gold price (around $4,000-4,100/oz) enabling larger ticket sizes (INR8-10 lakh working capital); thesis weakens if gold falls to about $2,500.

AI voice and text bots disbursed INR2,500 crore in Q1, targeted at INR11,000-12,000 crore for FY27; voice bot and data-driven originations about 20% of consumer PL in a month (INR4,000-6,000 crore monthly).

Smartphone industry shipments down 13-15% QoQ per counterpoint, but company smartphone volumes up 20-23% on Apple mix and ticket size up 32-33%; appliance ticket sizes roughly flat, AC prices affected by GST cut.
ETB share of customers now 63%, up from about 60%; app-based customers about 70% ETB and 30% NTB.

qa_highlights.question: Given the strong Q1, why is FY27 guidance unchanged, and could AUM growth beat 22-24% and credit cost come in at the lower end?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Jain said Q1 is much better than March guidance on AUM, PBT, ROA and ROE, but wants Q2 confirmation before revising guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR296 crore overlay recur, and will it be used to strengthen the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to strengthen balance sheet resilience and bulletproof it, with more clarity on the overlay direction and FY27 guidance after one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is improvement in credit cost structural or cyclical, and does it imply yield compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Jain said risk choices drive outcomes, not macro; risk thresholds are 30-40% of industry bureau delinquency; lower credit costs are accelerating growth.

qa_highlights.question: What share of disbursements comes from AI/digital channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Voice bots contribute about 17-18% of monthly consumer PL originations; voice and data together about 20%; digital platform is 25% of gold loans and about 20% of business loans.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds outlook and liquidity strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of funds up 30-60 bps; stabilised since September; Anand Bagri expects range-bound with slight upward bias; liability maturity longer than asset maturity.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI opex controlled, and is open source or SLM used?
qa_highlights.answer: Anurag Chottani said AI cost must be below human cost (voice AI about one-third of human cost); uses open-source models, internal RAG infrastructure and small/mini models rather than full LLMs.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and capital position given leverage at 4.9x?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Jain guided NIM moderation of 10-15 bps; capital adequacy at 21%; BHFL dilution from 86.7% to 75% is the first protocol; no capital raise foreseen unless growth accelerates.

qa_highlights.question: Can ROE reach 24% and ROA exceed 5% over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is possible to maximise, but prefers sustainable growth reinvestment; expects ROE improvement in Q2 after dividend payout; sees scale to INR10-12 lakh crore AUM without dilution.

risks_watch: Geopolitical tensions (West Asia crisis) and monsoon uncertainty (possible El Nino) could drive inflation, higher cost of funds and further macro overlays.
Cost of funds could rise further (30-60 bps incremental) and margin moderation of 10-15 bps is guided.
Gold loan competition from banks and new entrants, and gold price sensitivity (business economics weaken below about $2,500/oz).
Rising AI token and deployment costs; management flagged this as a line to watch.
MSME recovery timing (expected by about Q3 FY27); BHFL competitive attrition; SKU price increases from OEMs.
Management term decision Dec 2027 to Jan 2028; BHFL dilution timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on quarter performance and momentum, but deliberately cautious on forward guidance, deferring revisions to Q2 and repeatedly citing geopolitical and monsoon risks. Evasive on the ROE/ROA ambition and the margin question, with long reinvestment and resilience framing.
key_quotes: Excellent quarter, I would say. I mean, I've used this word after a long time, probably six - seven quarters, across all metrics actually, volume momentum, new customer addition.
Risk doesn't hold the company back. It propels the company forward.
Give us one more quarter we will provide greater clarity on guidance for the year and direction of overlay creation.
We are very clear the choice we are making is to being the lowest risk company in India.

growth.why: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 22-24% is held (not raised), with gold loan AUM of INR29,000-31,000 crore and 2,700-2,800 branches by year-end backing growth; Q1 profit grew 28% and a record INR37,000 crore AUM was added, but management defers guidance revision to Q2.
